Add conflict or protest data to a state panel

Source: R/add_data.R
add_conflict.Rd

Joins a conflict, protest, or revolutionary episode dataset onto an existing state panel. The panel's coding system and time unit (year, month, or day; see build_states_panel()) are detected automatically, and the data are aggregated to that unit.

Event and conflict-year datasets ("scad", "ucdp_prio", "ucdp_vpp", "mm", "mmad", "arc", "navco3.0") are already aggregated to the panel's unit when loaded, so the aggregate argument has no effect for them.

Campaign and episode datasets ("navco1.3", "navco2.1", "beissinger", "raqed", "mec", and "omg") can have multiple rows per country-period. With aggregate = TRUE (the default) these are collapsed to the panel's unit by taking the maximum of all numeric columns, and an n_campaigns count column is added. Set aggregate = FALSE to keep campaign-level rows (may produce duplicates). Onset columns mark the period in which an episode started; for all of these datasets, <prefix>incidence and <prefix>n_active also mark every period in which an episode was in progress, from its start to its end date (see Details).

Usage

add_conflict(panel, dataset, aggregate = TRUE, fill_zero = FALSE)

Arguments

panel

A data frame produced by build_states_panel().

dataset

Dataset to load. One of:

"navco1.3"

NAVCO 1.3 campaign onsets (1900-2019).

"navco2.1"

NAVCO 2.1 campaign-years (1945-2013).

"beissinger"

Beissinger revolutionary episode onsets (1900-2014).

"raqed"

RAQED v1.4 revolutionary and quasi-revolutionary episodes (2000-2026). Prefix: raqed_.

"scad"

SCAD 2018 social conflict events, Africa and Latin America (recorded starts 1989-2017). Prefix: scad_.

"ucdp_prio"

UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset v26.1 (1946-2025). Prefix: ucdp_prio_.

"ucdp_vpp"

UCDP Violent Political Protest v26.1 (1989-2025). Prefix: ucdp_vpp_. Requires the readxl package.

"mm"

Mass Mobilization Project v4 (1990-2020). Prefix: mm_.

"mmad"

Mass Mobilization in Autocracies Database (2003-2022). Prefix: mmad_.

"mec"

Major Episodes of Contention (1955-2018), with global episode-level coverage. Prefix: mec_.

"omg"

Opposition Movements and Groups v1, campaign phases (1789-2019). omg_onset marks a campaign's first phase. Prefix: omg_.

"arc"

Anatomy of Resistance Campaigns 2.0 events with participating organizations, Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean (1990-2018). Prefix: arc_.

"navco3.0"

NAVCO 3.0 events on 26 countries (1990-2012): actions by anti-government campaigns, states, and others, with tactics, goals, and state responses. Prefix: nvc3.0_.

aggregate

Logical. If TRUE (default), aggregates to the panel's unit before joining (relevant for campaign and episode datasets only). If FALSE, performs a raw left join.

fill_zero

Logical. If FALSE (default), periods without a record are NA. If TRUE, event indicators and counts (onset, incidence, and count columns) are set to 0 in periods the dataset covers but in which it records nothing, and stay NA outside its coverage. See Details and list_datasets() for how coverage is defined.

Value

The input panel with conflict/protest columns added via left join. With fill_zero = FALSE, unmatched periods remain NA; the function does not assume that an unobserved event indicator is zero.

Details

Coverage and fill_zero. A missing record can mean that nothing happened or that the source does not cover that country and year. With fill_zero = TRUE, a country-year counts as covered by these rules:

  • Global datasets ("navco1.3", "navco2.1", "beissinger", "raqed", "mec", "omg", "ucdp_prio", "ucdp_vpp"): every state in the panel, within the dataset's years.

  • Regional datasets ("scad", "arc", "navco3.0"): the countries with at least one record, within the dataset's years.

  • "mm": the country-years the source lists, including those it codes as having no protest.

  • "mmad": MMAD covers autocracies, and the package does not ship its list of autocratic country-years; a country counts as covered from the first to the last year in which MMAD records an event there. A 0 inside that span can therefore still be a period the source did not code (for example, MMAD has no events in Egypt from July to December 2012).

Only indicators and counts are filled (columns ending in _onset, _incidence, _episode, _n_*, or _total, n_campaigns, the UCDP conflict-type indicators, and NAVCO 3.0 fatalities and injuries). Maxima, means, and descriptive columns stay NA in periods without records. Coverage is decided by year, so in finer panels every period of a covered year is covered.

Active episodes. <prefix>incidence is 1 in every period in which at least one episode was in progress and <prefix>n_active counts them. An episode is in progress from its start to its end date. Start dates less precise than the panel's unit drop the episode, as for onsets. An end date less precise than the unit is taken to be the last day of the period the source gives: an OMG phase that ended "in 2005" is active through December 2005. Beissinger episodes end at the start date plus the source's duration (in days, or in calendar months for month-precise starts). Episodes the source codes as ongoing run to the end of its coverage. For "navco2.1", every campaign-year counts as active.

Dates. In a country-quarter, country-month, or country-day panel, each event or episode onset is placed in the period of its start date. Records whose source date is less precise than the panel's unit (for example, an OMG phase dated only to a year in a country-month panel) are dropped with a message. "navco1.3", "navco2.1", "ucdp_prio", and "ucdp_vpp" record only years and are available for country-year panels only.

Examples

# Country-month panel of protest events
monthly <- build_states_panel(2010, 2012, coding_system = "cow", unit = "month") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "mmad")

# 0 instead of NA where the dataset covers the country but records nothing
monthly <- build_states_panel(2010, 2012, coding_system = "cow", unit = "month") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "navco3.0", fill_zero = TRUE)

# Episodes in progress, not only their onsets
panel <- build_states_panel(2000, 2020, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "raqed")
#> Multiple campaigns or episodes per country-year detected in 'raqed'. Aggregating to country-year using max() for numeric columns. Use `aggregate = FALSE` or `conflict_data()` for record-level data.
panel[panel$cow == 652, c("year", "raqed_onset", "raqed_incidence")]
#>      year raqed_onset raqed_incidence
#> 2651 2000          NA              NA
#> 2652 2001          NA              NA
#> 2653 2002          NA              NA
#> 2654 2003          NA              NA
#> 2655 2004          NA              NA
#> 2656 2005          NA              NA
#> 2657 2006          NA              NA
#> 2658 2007          NA              NA
#> 2659 2008          NA              NA
#> 2660 2009          NA              NA
#> 2661 2010          NA              NA
#> 2662 2011           1               1
#> 2663 2012           1               1
#> 2664 2013          NA               1
#> 2665 2014           1               1
#> 2666 2015          NA               1
#> 2667 2016          NA               1
#> 2668 2017          NA               1
#> 2669 2018          NA               1
#> 2670 2019          NA               1
#> 2671 2020          NA               1

panel <- build_states_panel(1990, 2010, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "navco2.1")
#> Multiple campaigns or episodes per country-year detected in 'navco2.1'. Aggregating to country-year using max() for numeric columns. Use `aggregate = FALSE` or `conflict_data()` for record-level data.

panel <- build_states_panel(1990, 2010, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "ucdp_prio")

panel <- build_states_panel(2005, 2020, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "mmad")

# Raw join for legacy datasets — researcher handles aggregation manually
panel <- build_states_panel(1990, 2010, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "navco1.3", aggregate = FALSE)

# MEC is episode-level; keep individual episodes with aggregate = FALSE
panel <- build_states_panel(1990, 2010, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_conflict(dataset = "mec", aggregate = FALSE)
